_comment: Anything under overrides beats what the logo says and survives re-running brand:init. Use hex strings. brand, accent and feature are SOURCE colours: their relatives are derived from them, so pinning one of those three corrects everything downstream. The rest are pinned individually.
_why: Mt Cedar's palette predates this tool. It was chosen by a designer, not read off the crest, and extraction disagrees with it: clustering the crest yields green and RED, so an unpinned brand:init proposes a salmon accent and a purple feature band. The extractor is not wrong about the image, it is wrong about the brand, and no logo can tell it the difference. This file is what makes `npm run brand:init` reproduce the palette that is actually deployed instead of silently repainting a live school site. A NEW school will not need most of these: pin the two or three the extractor gets wrong and let the rest derive.
